rv.q: What he’s doing is simply structured, generously conceived, full—inside its simple container—of irresolvable yearning and wondering, guessing and risking — and it’s completely wonderful.
'School Pictures' is at once entertaining, educational, thought provoking, vulnerable, hilarious, sentimental, and heart-warming.
"School Pictures" is that rare one-person show: satisfying and original as well as honest in revealing child psychology as well as a teacher's perspective.

Milo Cramer is snagging the audience’s attention at Playwrights Horizons in ‘School Pictures’, a song cycle of 10 numbers, each pertaining to a youngster under Cramer’s tutoring...These intimate tutor-child interactions underpin the show’s critiques of the classist and racist education system that burdens children with inequities.
School Pictures -- a piece that ultimately becomes captivating -- might be a knockout.

Cramer accompanies himself first on a ukulele, then a tiny toy piano, then an electronic keyboard, and finally a real piano. It doesn't rhyme, it's basically recitative. And it's fun at first, but 70 minutes is a long time to sustain this sort of gambit, and by the end you wish he'd spoken more and sung less.

cn.t: Critics praise "School Pictures" for Milo Cramer's charming performance and poignant storytelling that blends humor with incisive critiques of educational inequity, creating an entertaining and thought-provoking one-person show.
